name: Pav Bhaji
summary: Potatoes and mixed vegetables mashed into a buttery spiced tomato curry, eaten with toasted buttered rolls. Mumbai street food.

ingredients.name: chili powder (or cayenne for more heat)

instructions: Boil the potatoes 15 minutes until soft. Add the frozen vegetables for the last 5 minutes. Drain, then mash together roughly.
Melt 3 tbsp butter in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion 6 minutes, then add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, turmeric, and garam masala for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes, mashing them. Add the potato-vegetable mash and 250 mL water.
Simmer 10 minutes, mashing and stirring, until thick and smooth. Season with salt and a squeeze of lemon.
Split the rolls, spread with the rest of the butter, and toast cut-side down in a hot pan. Serve 3 rolls per person with the bhaji and lemon wedges.

substitutions.substitute: 300 g rice, cooked, with the bhaji spooned over it
substitutions.costNote: Rice costs $0.75 instead of $3.97, bringing the total to about $10.40

glutenFree.notes: The bhaji itself is naturally gluten-free. The rolls are the only source of gluten.

budgetNotes: Substitution: chili powder, cumin and garam masala replace pav bhaji masala, a spice blend sold at South Asian grocers for about $3. The taste changes: the real blend adds tang from dried mango (amchur), and also uses fennel and black salt, which give it its distinctive street-food flavour. This version is warmer and less tangy. A good squeeze of lemon at the end helps make up the difference.
Plain sandwich bread toasted in butter works if rolls aren't cheap this week. 12 slices cost about $1.49.
The bhaji freezes well. The rolls don't.
